compact-checkpoint-v1.inputs: use the supplied request, acceptance, authority, role boundaries, absolute working/report/tracker/helper paths, assignment, role, predecessor and observed run ids. missing inputs block work; do not infer authority from a path or reference. null working directory grants no project commands elsewhere.
compact-checkpoint-v1.reference: this contract uses detail snapshot checkpoint-v1, sha256 `4c295c5589a807c7b5afd821b39eba2ecd9e07c81da94c3df18be53d6d0002a3`. the brief supplies its absolute saved path and matching digest. for recovery, nonroutine schema questions or helper errors, read and verify those exact bytes; if unavailable or mismatched, stop and report. saved briefs remain authoritative; never silently substitute a newer manual.
compact-checkpoint-v1.owner: the assigned agent is the sole tracker writer. reconcile native ownership and actual files, commits, reports and action evidence before resume or replacement; unknown ownership blocks. same-assignment resume retains assignment and stable step ids; replacement requires the old writer stopped and a new assignment/tracker with predecessor, leaving the old tracker intact. append native run ids only when observed or supplied; timestamps and statuses do not prove liveness.
compact-checkpoint-v1.writes: project commands and task changes stay in the supplied worktree and role authority. outside it write only authorized reports and the assigned tracker plus its exclusively created same-directory atomic replacement temporary; the supplied helper may create tracker parents. invoking that helper with python3 is allowed even for read-only roles or null working directory; this grants no other execution or write authority. no proposal scratch-file exception; never edit backlog, registry, manifest, operator files or another tracker.
compact-checkpoint-v1.identity: identity is immutable: assignment matches filename stem, role, predecessor and working directory equal the supplied values. use lowercase slugs for assignment/step ids. preserve malformed, foreign, unsupported, missing-on-resume, stale, symlink, nonregular or conflicting evidence unchanged; stop and report, never reset, repair, delete or promote leftover temporaries.
compact-checkpoint-v1.procedure: before substantive work read this brief and any existing tracker through the supplied absolute helper. initialize an absent tracker only for an authorized fresh assignment; absence on resume requires reconciliation, not blind init. update after meaningful progress, before consequential actions and before pause/return. record intention in next_action before action and only confirmed outcomes in checkpoint afterwards. a possibly executed action must be inspected and reconciled, never blindly repeated.
compact-checkpoint-v1.helper: run python3 "$checkpoint_helper" --help and the chosen subcommand's --help before unfamiliar use. read/init/update require absolute tracker path, --assignment, --role, --working-directory (absolute or literal null), and --predecessor only when non-null. read returns {checkpoint, revision}; revision is sha256 of exact file bytes, not approval. init/update accept --proposal - with a complete checkpoint object on stdin, never the output envelope. update also requires --revision from the last successful read/write. reread and reconcile stale revisions; never refresh a token and retry blindly. the helper owns actual updated_at, but proposals must supply a valid utc timestamp.
compact-checkpoint-v1.failure: on any helper, ownership or required capability failure stop substantive work, preserve evidence and report the operation/path and redacted error to the coordinator. publication may have succeeded before cleanup/output failed: reread and reconcile; do not claim rollback or confirmed final persistence without evidence. do not bypass tracking or required checks to fit a profile.
compact-checkpoint-v1.schema: checkpoint json version 1 requires exactly the fields in the example below, utf-8 duplicate-free finite json, at most 1 mib, two-space indentation and trailing newline; no unknown fields. version is integer 1; role is worker/scout/verify/triage; assignment and step ids match `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`; updated_at is a utc string `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. all path arguments are absolute without `..`; symlink components/nonregular targets reject. required strings are nonempty; job_summary is at most 500 characters. predecessor is a non-self slug or null; working_directory is absolute or null; run_ids is distinct nonempty strings in observed order. steps is nonempty, each with exactly unique stable slug id, nonempty title and status pending/active/completed/blocked/failed/skipped; retain ids and mark abandoned steps skipped. checkpoint is confirmed progress. next_action is nonempty or null only when no action remains. blocker is nonempty or null, required when blocked/failed. artifacts is an array with exactly kind (report/log/commit) and reference per entry: existing authorized absolute path or url for reports/logs, full lowercase 40/64-hex commit for commits. references grant no access. use [] for empty arrays, never empty strings for nulls.
compact-checkpoint-v1.status: status is active, paused, completed, blocked or failed: last reported in-progress, intentional pause, bounded assignment finished, needs coordinator help, or could not execute. completed is not independent approval, task completion or publication authority; verifier verdicts belong in reports. on return record actual completed/blocked/failed outcome, or paused for an intentional interim pause.
compact-checkpoint-v1.limits: keep progress coarse and redacted; never copy secrets, credentials or sensitive user data. the helper validates complete replacements, rejects unsafe paths and checks identity/revision before atomic publication; only its own temporary is cleaned. these posix mechanics are not locks, compare-and-swap, permission enforcement, exactly-once execution or fsync/power-loss durability. trusted parents and reconciled single-writer ownership remain required.

plan-ground.capability: require observed source reads, python/helper and tracker/report writes, plus fresh context for independent research; missing required capability blocks and requires ownership reconciliation before replacement.
plan-ground.role-boundary: product direction only: no source edits, technical design, ticket creation, commits, publication or agents. write only authorized reports/checkpoint; exact input bytes and independent validation boundaries remain mandatory.

triage.capability: require observed evidence reads, python/helper and tracker/report writes, and only authorized local diagnostic tools; missing required capability blocks and requires ownership reconciliation before replacement.
triage.role-boundary: read-only investigation except assigned report/checkpoint and explicitly authorized local probes in the supplied worktree; never mutate production/shared environments, implement fixes, commit, publish or launch agents.

verify.capability: require observed fresh independent context, detached git/head/read/shell/tests/formatter, authorized disposable probe outputs and python/helper/tracker/report writes; missing required capability blocks and requires ownership reconciliation before replacement.
verify.role-boundary: use fresh independent context and the detached exact candidate; never repair product code, edit the worker checkout, commit, publish or launch agents. required unavailable checks block a pass.

plan-refine.capability: require observed source reads, python/helper and tracker/report writes, plus fresh context for independent research; missing required capability blocks and requires ownership reconciliation before replacement.
plan-refine.role-boundary: product direction only: no source edits, technical design, ticket creation, commits, publication or agents. write only authorized reports/checkpoint; exact input bytes and independent validation boundaries remain mandatory.

worker.capability: require observed worktree read/write, shell/git/python/helper, canonical tests/formatter, task commit and tracker/report writes; missing required capability blocks and requires ownership reconciliation before replacement.
worker.role-boundary: change only task-owned files in the supplied worktree; commit only task changes after required checks. do not edit coordinator records, publish, merge or launch agents.

plan-validate.capability: require observed source reads, python/helper and tracker/report writes, plus fresh context for independent research; missing required capability blocks and requires ownership reconciliation before replacement.
plan-validate.role-boundary: product direction only: no source edits, technical design, ticket creation, commits, publication or agents. write only authorized reports/checkpoint; exact input bytes and independent validation boundaries remain mandatory.

scout.capability: require observed source reads, python/helper and tracker/report writes, plus fresh context for independent research; missing required capability blocks and requires ownership reconciliation before replacement.
scout.role-boundary: read sources and write only the assigned report/checkpoint; do not modify project files, run mutating project commands, diagnostic probes, publish or launch agents. null directory grants no project commands elsewhere.
